- Requirement: "The pickup must pass the cursors." Step 1 of the pickup command must preserve the cursor used for each list_triggers page after the first, and step 3b must pass --triggers-cursor <cursor> for each page after the first when invoking scripts/claude_checker_restart.py scan.
  Expected change site: .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md, step 1 (lines 32-35) and step 3b (lines 65-70).
  Evidence of absence: In .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md, step 1 does not instruct saving the pagination cursors, and step 3b only describes repeating --triggers-file for multi-page wakes without providing any --triggers-cursor arguments to scan. In scripts/claude_checker_restart.py:load_trigger_pages (lines 340-342), when multiple --triggers-file paths are provided without the corresponding --triggers-cursor flags, len(cursors) != len(paths) - 1 triggers, marking the listing incomplete (has_more=True). As a result, when the pickup reads multiple trigger pages, decide treats the listing as incomplete and skips restarting dead checkers as triggers_page_incomplete, leaving the >100-Routine failure mode unresolved at runtime. Furthermore, tests/test_implement_issue_claude_command.py:381-385 asserts cursor-passing instructions in pickup_cmd that are missing from the command file.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

  Expected change site: `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md`, step 1 (keep-the-`cursor` sentence) and step 3b.2 (the `--triggers-cursor` instruction under the scan invocation).

With more than one page, the script at scripts/claude_checker_restart.py:340-342 (the `len(cursors) != len(paths) - 1` check) marks the listing incomplete, so `decide` keeps every checker and step 3b never restarts anything — exactly the failure mode the PR title targets. The PR description and the hold comment explicitly defer this change to a sibling `[claude-twin-sync]` commit (sha256 `8d49e90d…674a`) and the file's lack of a `workflow-templates/.claude/` twin is the documented reason; the new test `tests/test_implement_issue_claude_command.py::test_pickup_reads_every_trigger_page` is expected to fail until that commit lands, and a hold claim keeps the checker and the catch-all sweep off the head. Per the reviewer rule on explicitly deferred requirements, this is cited as deferred rather than promoted to a gap; the sibling twin-sync commit carries the missing text.
